                    ### Question
                    A previously healthy 24-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-day history of painful rash after spending several hours in the sun. Skin examination shows well-demarcated areas of erythema with some scaling on the face, chest, upper back, and arms. The affected areas are hot and sensitive to touch. The oral mucosa appears normal. Which of the following is the most likely underlying mechanism of this patient's skin findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Vascular endothelial cell injury in the superficial dermis
opb. Immune complex deposits at the dermoepidermal junction
opc. Mast cell activation in the superficial dermis
opd. Apoptosis of keratinocytes in the epidermis
ope. T-cell-mediated inflammatory reaction in the dermis

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's presentation of a painful rash after sun exposure, characterized by erythema and scaling, suggests an inflammatory response likely due to UV radiation. The chains indicating 'T-cell-mediated inflammatory reaction in the dermis' are supported by the consensus that UV exposure can lead to keratinocyte damage and subsequent T-cell activation. The mechanisms involving apoptosis of keratinocytes and inflammatory cytokine release are also relevant, as they contribute to the recruitment of T-cells. While mast cell activation may play a role in some skin conditions, it is not the primary mechanism in this case. Therefore, the most likely underlying mechanism is a T-cell-mediated inflammatory reaction in the dermis, supported by the evidence of T-lymphocytes being part of the dermal inflammatory response.
